events.text: Among the prayers of your domain this year is one from {npc}, a farmer, who asked for rain. You sent rain. You sent rather a lot of rain, and {npc}'s whole valley is a lake.

choices.text: Go down and drain it yourself

effects.log: You stand in the valley and the water goes back into the hills like a rope drawn in. {npc} watches from the roof of the house and does not know what to pray now.

choices.text: Send {npc} fish

effects.log: If there is to be a lake, there should be fish in it. In a generation the valley is a fishing village, and {npc} is its headman.

choices.text: Let the valley learn to pray more exactly

effects.log: The temple scribes add a line to the prayer-forms about the amount of rain. Your faithful, you notice, have begun to be very specific.

events.text: {npc}'s valley has built a new shrine to you, half-sunk in the lake or high and dry on the hill, and the valley is arguing about what you meant by the flood. The priests say punishment. {npc} says a joke.

choices.text: Appear in a dream and say it was a mistake

effects.log: Gods do not usually admit mistakes. The valley is astonished and then devoted, and the priests rewrite their sermons.

choices.text: Let {npc} be right

effects.log: {npc} is right. The valley becomes known across your domain for laughing at festivals, and you find you enjoy its prayers most.

choices.text: Let the priests be right

effects.log: The valley becomes very well-behaved and rather dull. Its prayers come in neat rows, like taxes.

events.text: {npc}, a very small god, the god of one crossroads in the mortal world, has walked all the way up into the Divine Realm to ask for a place in your domain. The crossroads has become a town, and the town has stopped praying to {him}.
events.arc: The Small God of a Crossroads

choices.text: Take {npc} into your domain

effects.log: {npc} becomes the god of all the crossroads in your lands. It is a small office. {npc} takes it more seriously than any god you know.

choices.text: Go down and look at the town

effects.log: The town has a shrine to {npc} under a market stall, covered with baskets. You move the baskets. Three people notice, and pray.

choices.text: Tell {npc} that small gods last longest

effects.log: {npc} goes home thoughtful. A hundred years later the town is gone and the crossroads is still there, and so is {npc}.

events.text: A great god of your pantheon has noticed {npc} in your domain, or at the crossroads, and does not approve of small gods getting ideas. The great god demands {npc} be returned to the dust.
events.arc: The Small God of a Crossroads

choices.text: Stand between them

ok.log: The great god looks at you, looks at the small one, and decides it is not worth a quarrel. {npc} brings you a pebble from every crossroads, every year.

fail.log: The great god is stronger. You protect {npc} at the cost of a wound and a cold place in the pantheon.

choices.text: Make {npc} useful to the great god

effects.log: You arrange for {npc} to guard the crossroads of the great god's pilgrim road. The great god is delighted with this clever idea, which was yours.

choices.text: Let the pantheon decide

effects.log: The pantheon debates for ninety years and decides that small gods are allowed. {npc} is famous for a century as the god who caused the debate.

events.text: One of the stars of your domain has come loose and fallen into the mortal world, into a field. {npc}, a shepherd child, has found it, and is keeping it in a box under the bed because it is warm.

choices.text: Go down and ask for it back

effects.log: You ask politely. {npc} considers you, and the star, and says no. You find that you cannot argue with this.

choices.text: Let {npc} keep it

effects.log: The star lights the child's house for a lifetime. The village thinks the family is blessed. The family is.

choices.text: Take it back at night

effects.log: You take it. {npc} wakes in the morning to an empty box and cries for a week. The sky is whole. You are not sure it was worth it.

events.text: {npc} has grown up, and so has the star. It is too bright now for a box: it lights the whole valley at night, and the people of three villages have begun to pray to it, and not to you.

choices.text: Set the star back in the sky with {npc} watching

effects.log: You take {npc} up for one night. The star goes back where it belongs, and {npc} can point to it for the rest of a long life.

choices.text: Make {npc} its priest

effects.log: The star-shrine becomes part of your domain's faith, with {npc} at its door. The villages pray to both. You do not mind sharing.

choices.text: Let the valley have a star of its own

effects.log: The sky of your domain has one dark place in it now, and a valley in the mortal world has a light. It seems a fair trade.

events.text: Your priests report a valley in the far mountains that worships you with great devotion and gets everything wrong: your face, your name, your gifts. {npc}, their priest, has never met anyone from your temples and is very proud of the valley's version of you.
events.arc: A Valley That Worships You Wrong

choices.text: Visit the valley in disguise

effects.log: You are three times taller in their statues, and blue. You find it very touching. {npc} gives the stranger a guided tour.

choices.text: Send your priests to correct them

effects.log: Your priests correct them. The valley is hurt, and some of them stop praying. You think about that for a long time.

choices.text: Let the valley keep its own version

effects.log: Somewhere in your domain there is a blue god three times your height who loves the mountain goats. It is, you decide, also you.

events.text: The valley's version of you is spreading. Pilgrims come to the blue god, and some of your own priests are arguing that two of you is one too many. {npc} has written to ask which of you is real.
events.arc: A Valley That Worships You Wrong

choices.text: Write back: both

effects.log: {npc} frames the letter. The blue god and you share a feast day now. Your faith is a little stranger and a great deal larger.

choices.text: Go to the valley as yourself

effects.log: {npc} looks at you for a very long time, and then at the statue. "You are smaller," {npc} says. "We will keep the statue."

choices.text: Let the priests settle it

effects.log: The priests hold a council for thirty years and settle on a compromise nobody understands. The valley ignores it.

events.text: Something has come over the edge of your domain from the dark between the heavens: a host of hungry spirits led by {npc}, who was a god once, and is now very little but appetite.
variants: The far shrines of your domain go dark one by one, like lamps being pinched out. {npc}'s host is coming through the border-lands, eating faith as it goes.
A watcher at the edge of your domain sends word: {npc}, a fallen god, is gathering the lost and the hungry at your border, and the border is thin there.
The border-gods of your domain have gone silent one after another. Beyond them, in the dark, {npc} is leading a host that remembers being worshipped and wants it back.
A prayer comes up from the last village of your domain that is not a prayer, only a scream, and then nothing. {npc}'s host is at the edge.
Your faithful dream all on the same night of a grey tide coming over the hills. {npc}, a god who fell long ago, is walking at its head.
events.arc: At the Edge of the Domain

choices.text: Meet them at the border yourself

ok.log: The border holds. {npc}'s host scatters into the dark, and your faithful never know how close it came.

fail.log: You drive them back, but they take a bite out of you on the way. Your domain is dim for a season while you mend.

choices.text: Call on your pantheon for help

effects.log: Three gods come. The host is driven off. Now you owe three gods a favour each, and gods remember.

choices.text: Speak to {npc}, who was a god once

effects.log: You ask {npc} what was lost. It takes an age. At the end there is a little less appetite in the dark, and a little more grief, which is better.

events.text: {npc}, a god of a neighbouring domain, has been taking your worshippers: one village at a time, with better miracles and worse intentions. Today {npc} has come to tell you so in person.
variants: The priests of your domain report miracles that are not yours on your side of the border. {npc}, the god of the next domain, has stopped pretending not to be poaching.
{npc}'s priests have begun preaching in your temples, politely, on your own feast days. {npc} has come to see how you will take it.
A whole city of your domain has turned its faith to {npc} in a single season, and {npc} has sent you a gift to mark the occasion: a bell from its temple.

choices.text: Settle it god to god

ok.log: It shakes the mountains of three worlds and is over by evening. {npc} withdraws, and the villages come home.

fail.log: {npc} is stronger this age. You lose the exchange and two villages, and {npc} gloats for a century.

choices.text: Win the villages back with better gifts

effects.log: A good harvest, a cured fever, a well where there was none. The villages come home by themselves, and {npc} is left with nothing to say.

choices.text: Propose a border and a feast-day treaty

effects.log: {npc} accepts, sourly. The border is kept for an age, and the feast is surprisingly pleasant.

events.text: The prayers of your domain pile up like leaves. Most are for rain, sons, daughters, a cure or a little luck. One, this year, is from {npc}, who asks for nothing at all, only to say thank you.
variants: Among this year's prayers: {npc}, who has prayed to you every day for sixty years, asks for the first time for something of {his} own: one more spring.
A child in your domain, {npc}, has prayed to you for a puppy. The prayer is very detailed about the puppy. The temple priests, who read it, are smiling.

choices.text: Answer {npc} in a dream

effects.log: You thank {npc} back. {npc} wakes up and tells nobody, and is happy for a month for no reason {he} can name.

choices.text: Answer every prayer in the pile for a year

effects.log: A year of small miracles. Your domain glows. You are very tired at the end of it, and very loved.

choices.text: Send {npc} something unasked

effects.log: A lost ring turns up. An old pain stops. {npc} never connects these with the prayer, which is how it should be.

events.text: An envoy from another pantheon, {npc}, arrives at your domain with gifts and a proposal: an alliance, a marriage of two lesser gods, or a war against a third pantheon, depending on how the conversation goes.
variants: {npc} of the far pantheons arrives on a cloud the colour of bronze, with a hundred attendants and a list of grievances about a river you share.

choices.text: Hear the whole proposal

effects.log: It takes a month, because envoys of that pantheon only speak at dawn. At the end you have a treaty, a lesser alliance and a headache.

choices.text: Send {npc} home with better gifts than {he} brought

effects.log: It is a gesture the other pantheon understands. Your name is spoken warmly there for an age.

choices.text: Refuse every part of it, courteously

effects.log: {npc} leaves with nothing and admiration. "You are the first god who has said no to us all at once," {npc} says.

events.text: A mortal has climbed into the Divine Realm by a road nobody has used in an age. {npc} is ragged, half-frozen and furious, and has come to complain to a god in person about the state of the world.
variants: {npc}, a mortal scholar, has walked a road of clouds for nine years to ask a god one question: why there is suffering. {npc} has brought notes.

choices.text: Hear the complaint

effects.log: It is a long complaint, and fair. You change three things in your domain because of it. {npc} goes home and never knows.

choices.text: Feed {npc} first, then hear it

effects.log: After soup the complaint is shorter and kinder. {npc} goes home with a story nobody believes.

choices.text: Send {npc} back down with a gift

effects.log: A seed that will grow into a tree that never fails. {npc} plants it in the middle of the village, still grumbling.

events.text: A great beast of the Divine Realm, older than your godhood, has wandered into your domain and is eating your faithful's dreams. Mortals in three cities have stopped dreaming at all.
variants: Something huge is grazing on the clouds over your highest temple, and every grain of incense lit beneath it goes out.
A beast of the wild heavens has come down into your domain to calve, and while it calves it eats prayers. Your temples are going quiet one by one.
Something enormous is drinking from the river of offerings that runs through your domain. Downstream, the shrines are running dry.
Children in your domain have started to draw the same thing: a beast with seven eyes sitting on the clouds over the temple. It is there. It is hungry.

choices.text: Hunt it

ok.log: A chase across the sky for a month. You drive it back to the wild heavens, and the cities dream again, very vividly, for a year.

fail.log: It is older and stronger than you thought. You turn it out of your domain, but it marks you as it goes.

choices.text: Feed it your own dreams instead

effects.log: It eats them slowly and leaves content. You do not dream for a century. You find you do not miss it as much as you feared.

choices.text: Lead it gently to a pantheon that worships it

effects.log: It is a god there. It is very happy. Your cities dream again.

events.text: An age has turned since you took your domain. The faithful who first prayed to you are a legend among their own descendants, and some of your temples are older than the cities around them.
variants: The oldest prayer-book of your domain has been copied so many times that a word in it has changed. Your faithful now pray to you for patience instead of rain. You find you like it.

choices.text: Walk among your oldest temples

effects.log: You walk them in a single night. Some have fallen, some have grown. In one, a child is asleep on the altar, and you let the child sleep.

choices.text: Renew your covenant with the faithful

effects.log: A sign in every temple at once: a bell that rings by itself. Faith rises like a tide across the domain.

choices.text: Let the age turn quietly

effects.log: You do nothing, and watch. A god, you think, should sometimes be the one who does nothing and watches.

events.text: {npc}, a lesser god of your own domain, the god of its western hills, has been taking more faith than the hills give, and this age has said aloud at a feast that the domain needs a younger god.

choices.text: Answer {npc} at the feast

ok.log: You stand. The hall goes silent. {npc} feels what you are and sits down, and stays the god of the western hills, a little smaller.

fail.log: {npc} has grown stronger than you knew. You put {him} down, but the feast sees you bleed, and the domain talks.

choices.text: Give {npc} more to do

effects.log: You give {npc} the eastern marshes too. Two domains of faith keep {him} very busy, and very loyal.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what the hills need

effects.log: The hills are dying: a drought, a failing faith. You help. {npc} never speaks of younger gods again.

variants: {npc}, god of your western hills, has begun to call the hills a domain, and the hill-folk have started to pray past you, straight to {him}.
At the feast of your domain {npc} has taken the seat next to yours, which is not {his}, and is smiling at the other gods as if it were.

events.text: Faith casts a shadow. In a city of your domain, the prayers of fear have pooled into something with your face and none of your mercy, and it is answering prayers in your name.

choices.text: Face your shadow

ok.log: It is you, as the frightened see you. You beat it, and it is smaller every time you look at the city after.

fail.log: It knows everything you know. You win only by refusing to fight as it fights, and come away hurt and very thoughtful.

choices.text: Give the city reasons not to be afraid

effects.log: A year of small mercies. The shadow thins and goes out, like a lamp with no oil.

choices.text: Speak to the city in its dreams

effects.log: You tell them who you are. Some of them believe you. It is enough to starve the shadow, slowly.

variants: In a city of your domain a figure in your robes walks the streets at night and grants the wishes of the frightened, all of them, exactly, cruelly.
Your priests report a new image in one city's shrine: your face, but with teeth. The people say it answers faster than you do.
